title: 1 Kings Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Kings chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Kings Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Kings Chapter 1.

questions.question: What was the condition of King David as described at the beginning of 1 Kings chapter 1?
options: He was young and energetic
He was old and stricken in years
He was traveling to another city
He was leading an army
questions.correctAnswer: He was old and stricken in years
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:1 states that King David was old and stricken in years.

questions.question: What did David's servants suggest to help the king get heat?
options: They suggested building a fire
They suggested finding a young virgin to stand before the king
They suggested moving to a warmer place
They suggested giving him warm clothes
questions.correctAnswer: They suggested finding a young virgin to stand before the king
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 1:2, the servants said to seek a young virgin to stand before the king and cherish him.

questions.question: Who was the young woman brought to minister to King David?
options: Abigail the Carmelite
Abishag the Shunammite
Michal the daughter of Saul
Bathsheba the wife of Uriah
questions.correctAnswer: Abishag the Shunammite
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:3 identifies Abishag the Shunammite as the young woman brought to the king.

questions.question: True or False: King David knew Abishag, the young woman who ministered to him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:4 clearly states that the king knew her not.

questions.question: Who exalted himself saying, 'I will be king'?
options: Solomon the son of David
Adonijah the son of Haggith
Joab the son of Zeruiah
Nathan the prophet
questions.correctAnswer: Adonijah the son of Haggith
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:5 states that Adonijah exalted himself saying, 'I will be king.'

questions.question: What did Adonijah prepare for himself to show his claim to kingship?
options: A palace and throne
Chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him
A large army of foreign mercenaries
A special feast for the elders
questions.correctAnswer: Chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:5 describes Adonijah preparing chariots, horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.

questions.question: True or False: King David was displeased with Adonijah for his actions.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:6 indicates that David had not displeased Adonijah or questioned him about his actions.

questions.question: Which two men did Adonijah confer with to gain support?
options: Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet
Joab the son of Zeruiah and Abiathar the priest
Benaiah and Shimei
Nathan the prophet and Benaiah
questions.correctAnswer: Joab the son of Zeruiah and Abiathar the priest
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:7 tells us that Adonijah conferred with Joab and Abiathar, who helped him.

questions.question: True or False: Zadok the priest, Benaiah, and Nathan supported Adonijah.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:8 states that Zadok, Benaiah, Nathan, and others were not with Adonijah.

questions.question: Where did Adonijah slaughter animals and call his brethren and servants?
options: At the tabernacle in Shiloh
By the stone of Zoheleth, which is by Enrogel
In the palace of David
On Mount Zion
questions.correctAnswer: By the stone of Zoheleth, which is by Enrogel
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:9 records that Adonijah slew animals by the stone of Zoheleth near Enrogel.

questions.question: Who did Adonijah notably not call to his feast?
options: All the king's servants
Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty men, and Solomon
His mother Haggith
Joab the captain of the host
questions.correctAnswer: Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty men, and Solomon
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:10 says Adonijah did not call Nathan, Benaiah, the mighty men, or Solomon.

questions.question: Who spoke to Bathsheba about Adonijah's actions?
options: Joab the captain
Abiathar the priest
Nathan the prophet
Benaiah the son of Jehoiada
questions.correctAnswer: Nathan the prophet
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:11 shows Nathan speaking to Bathsheba about Adonijah reigning without David's knowledge.

questions.question: What counsel did Nathan give Bathsheba?
options: To flee the city for safety
To go to King David and remind him of his promise about Solomon
To prepare an army to fight Adonijah
To ignore Adonijah's actions
questions.correctAnswer: To go to King David and remind him of his promise about Solomon
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:12-13 shows Nathan advising Bathsheba to remind the king of his oath that Solomon shall reign after him.

questions.question: True or False: Bathsheba went to King David to speak with him as Nathan advised.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:15 states that Bathsheba went in unto the king as Nathan had counseled.

questions.question: What did Bathsheba remind King David about during her visit?
options: That Adonijah was making offerings to the LORD
That David had sworn that Solomon would reign after him
That the kingdom was under threat from enemies
That the servants needed a new leader
questions.correctAnswer: That David had sworn that Solomon would reign after him
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:17 shows Bathsheba reminding David of his oath that Solomon would sit on his throne.

medium.title: 1 Kings Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Kings Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Nathan the prophet ask King David regarding Adonijah's claim to the throne?
options: If David had said Adonijah shall reign after him
If Solomon was already crowned king
If Bathsheba supported Adonijah
If Joab was aware of the situation
questions.correctAnswer: If David had said Adonijah shall reign after him
questions.explanation: Nathan questioned David whether he had declared that Adonijah would reign after him, highlighting the issue of rightful succession (1 Kings 1:24). This is connected to the larger context where Adonijah had exalting himself without David's consent (1 Kings 1:5-7).

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 1:19 describe the gathering Adonijah held?
options: He called all the king's sons, Abiathar the priest, and Joab the captain of the host
He gathered only Solomon's supporters
He invited foreign dignitaries
He held a secret meeting with Nathan the prophet
questions.correctAnswer: He called all the king's sons, Abiathar the priest, and Joab the captain of the host
questions.explanation: Adonijah summoned the king's sons and key leaders such as Abiathar and Joab but notably excluded Solomon (1 Kings 1:19), which was part of his attempt to claim the throne (1 Kings 1:9-10).

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 1:20, what responsibility does King David have regarding the throne?
options: To declare who will sit on the throne after him
To build a new palace for Solomon
To exile Adonijah
To appoint Joab as captain
questions.correctAnswer: To declare who will sit on the throne after him
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that all Israel looks to King David to declare the rightful successor, underscoring the importance of his decision for national stability (1 Kings 1:20). This follows the concern raised about Adonijah's premature reign (1 Kings 1:19).

questions.question: What consequence does Nathan warn Bathsheba about if the rightful king is not declared, according to 1 Kings 1:21?
options: She and Solomon would be considered offenders
Adonijah would be crowned by force
David would lose his throne
Joab would rebel
questions.correctAnswer: She and Solomon would be considered offenders
questions.explanation: Nathan warns that failure to establish Solomon's kingship would result in Bathsheba and Solomon being seen as offenders after David's death (1 Kings 1:21), highlighting the need for clear succession to avoid injustice (1 Kings 1:20).

questions.question: How did Bathsheba approach King David when she came to speak with him, as described in 1 Kings 1:16 and 1 Kings 1:28?
options: She bowed and did obeisance before the king
She demanded the throne for Solomon
She refused to speak until Solomon was present
She brought a large crowd to support her
questions.correctAnswer: She bowed and did obeisance before the king
questions.explanation: Bathsheba respectfully bowed and showed reverence before King David (1 Kings 1:16, 1 Kings 1:28), demonstrating humility and respect in presenting her petition about Solomon's rightful succession (1 Kings 1:17-18).

questions.question: What oath did King David reaffirm to Bathsheba concerning Solomon's future, according to 1 Kings 1:30?
options: That Solomon shall reign after him and sit on his throne
That Adonijah will be the next king
That Nathan will anoint Solomon secretly
That Joab will be made captain of the host
questions.correctAnswer: That Solomon shall reign after him and sit on his throne
questions.explanation: David swore by the LORD God of Israel that Solomon will certainly succeed him and sit on his throne, reaffirming the promise made previously (1 Kings 1:30). This confirms the legitimacy of Solomon's claim against Adonijah's self-exaltation (1 Kings 1:5-6).

questions.question: What instructions did King David give to Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah regarding Solomon's kingship in 1 Kings 1:33-35?
options: Bring Solomon to Gihon, anoint him king, and proclaim him with trumpets
Hide Solomon until Adonijah dies
Prepare Solomon's army for battle
Send Solomon to Egypt for safety
questions.correctAnswer: Bring Solomon to Gihon, anoint him king, and proclaim him with trumpets
questions.explanation: David commanded that Solomon be brought to Gihon, anointed by Zadok and Nathan, and proclaimed king with trumpet blasts, establishing his legitimate reign publicly (1 Kings 1:33-35). This was to counter Adonijah's earlier self-declaration as king (1 Kings 1:9-10).

questions.question: How did Benaiah respond to King David's command about Solomon's kingship in 1 Kings 1:36?
options: He said, Amen, and prayed for Solomon's throne to be greater
He refused to support Solomon
He suggested waiting until Adonijah agreed
He asked for more time to prepare
questions.correctAnswer: He said, Amen, and prayed for Solomon's throne to be greater
questions.explanation: Benaiah enthusiastically agreed, saying 'Amen' and prayed that the LORD would make Solomon's throne greater than David's (1 Kings 1:36-37), showing faithful support and trust in God's plan for leadership.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Kings 1:25-26, Adonijah invited Nathan the prophet, Zadok the priest, and Solomon to his feast.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Adonijah called all the king's sons, captains, and Abiathar the priest to his feast but did not call Nathan, Zadok, or Solomon (1 Kings 1:25-26), indicating a political move to exclude Solomon and his supporters.

questions.question: True or False: The people rejoiced loudly and blew trumpets when Solomon was anointed king as described in 1 Kings 1:39-40.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: When Solomon was anointed by Zadok, the people blew trumpets and rejoiced with great joy, causing the earth to be rent with the sound, showing public approval (1 Kings 1:39-40).

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 1:20 teach about the importance of leadership clarity in Israel?
options: All Israel's eyes are on the king to know who will succeed him
The priests should decide the next king
The people want to choose the king by vote
The army should support the strongest son
questions.correctAnswer: All Israel's eyes are on the king to know who will succeed him
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that the entire nation looks to David for clear direction on the rightful successor to maintain order and unity (1 Kings 1:20), which is vital for faithful leadership and peace.

questions.question: Based on 1 Kings 1:31 and 1 Kings 1:48, how does King David express his feelings about Solomon's kingship?
options: He blesses Solomon and praises the LORD for allowing him to see this day
He regrets not naming Adonijah
He remains silent and weak
He fears for Solomon's future
questions.correctAnswer: He blesses Solomon and praises the LORD for allowing him to see this day
questions.explanation: David blesses Solomon, expressing reverence and joy, and praises God for granting him the sight to witness Solomon's accession (1 Kings 1:31, 1 Kings 1:48), showing faith, gratitude, and humility.

questions.question: What does the scenario in 1 Kings 1:19-21 teach about the importance of obedience and trust in God's plan for leadership?
options: Disobedience to rightful authority can cause division and guilt
Everyone should seek power regardless of God's will
Secret alliances guarantee success
Ignoring God's chosen leader is harmless
questions.correctAnswer: Disobedience to rightful authority can cause division and guilt
questions.explanation: Adonijah's self-exaltation without David's approval brings fear and potential offense (1 Kings 1:19-21), illustrating that trusting God's plan and obeying rightful leadership prevents conflict and dishonor.

questions.question: What practical lesson about integrity can be learned from Benaiah's response in 1 Kings 1:36-37?
options: Supporting God's anointed leader with faith leads to blessing and honor
Remaining neutral is the best course
Opposing the king is always right
Power should be seized by force
questions.correctAnswer: Supporting God's anointed leader with faith leads to blessing and honor
questions.explanation: Benaiah's affirmation and prayer for Solomon's throne reflect integrity and faithfulness to God's choice, demonstrating the blessing that comes from loyal support (1 Kings 1:36-37).

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Kings 1:27, Nathan questioned whether King David had informed him about who should sit on the throne after him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Nathan asked David if he had shown him who should succeed him, indicating concern about David's silence on the matter (1 Kings 1:27). This highlights the need for clear communication in leadership transitions.

hard.title: 1 Kings Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Kings Chapter 1.

questions.question: Who anointed Solomon king over Israel at Gihon as described in 1 Kings 1?
options: Zadok the priest
Nathan the prophet
Benaiah the son of Jehoiada
All of the above
questions.correctAnswer: Zadok the priest
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:39 specifically states that Zadok the priest took a horn of oil and anointed Solomon king at Gihon.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the people when Solomon was anointed king according to 1 Kings 1?
options: They were silent
They shouted 'God save king Solomon'
They mourned
They argued among themselves
questions.correctAnswer: They shouted 'God save king Solomon'
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 1:39, after Solomon's anointing, the trumpet was blown and all the people said, 'God save king Solomon.'

questions.question: Which two groups accompanied Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah when they brought Solomon to Gihon?
options: Cherethites and Pelethites
Levites and Priests
Prophets and Elders
Judahites and Ephraimites
questions.correctAnswer: Cherethites and Pelethites
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:38 states that the Cherethites and Pelethites went with Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah to bring Solomon to Gihon.

questions.question: What does Solomon's throne being made greater than David's symbolize in a broader biblical context?
options: The continuation and expansion of the Davidic covenant
The end of the monarchy in Israel
The rejection of God's promises
The rise of the priesthood over kingship
questions.correctAnswer: The continuation and expansion of the Davidic covenant
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:37 and 1:47 mention Solomon's throne being greater than David's, reflecting God's covenant in 2 Samuel 7:12-16 where David's dynasty is promised an eternal kingdom.

questions.question: What literary device is notably used in the narrative of Solomon’s anointing and the reaction of the city?
options: Chiasmus
Parable
Allegory
Foreshadowing
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus
questions.explanation: The structure in 1 Kings 1:38-40 shows a chiastic pattern emphasizing the procession, anointing, and rejoicing, reinforcing the legitimacy of Solomon’s kingship, a common literary device in Hebrew narrative.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'horn of oil' used for anointing Solomon in 1 Kings 1:39?
options: It symbolizes the Holy Spirit and divine approval
It was used to purify the king physically
It was a gift from foreign nations
It signifies wealth and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the Holy Spirit and divine approval
questions.explanation: Anointing with oil, especially from a horn as mentioned in 1 Kings 1:39, denotes setting apart by God, similar to other anointings like in 1 Samuel 10:1 and Psalms 133:2.

questions.question: Who was the first to inform Adonijah about Solomon’s anointing and kingship?
options: Jonathan son of Abiathar
Joab
Nathan the prophet
Benaiah
questions.correctAnswer: Jonathan son of Abiathar
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 1:42-43, Jonathan, son of Abiathar the priest, came to Adonijah and told him that David had made Solomon king.

questions.question: What was Adonijah's reaction upon hearing the trumpet and learning about Solomon's kingship?
options: He celebrated with his guests
He fled the city
He caught hold of the horns of the altar
He immediately confronted Solomon
questions.correctAnswer: He caught hold of the horns of the altar
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:50 shows that Adonijah feared Solomon and took refuge by catching hold of the horns of the altar seeking protection.

questions.question: What promise did Solomon make to Adonijah after he took refuge at the altar?
options: To spare his life if he proved himself worthy
To exile him from the kingdom
To execute him immediately
To grant him a share of the kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: To spare his life if he proved himself worthy
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:52 records Solomon saying that if Adonijah showed himself a worthy man, not a hair of him would fall to the earth, but if wickedness was found, he would die.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is connected to the promise of Solomon's greater throne mentioned in 1 Kings 1:37?
options: 2 Samuel 7:12-16
Genesis 12:1-3
Exodus 20:1-17
Psalm 23
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Samuel 7:12-16
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 7:12-16 contains God's covenant with David promising his offspring's throne will be established forever, which 1 Kings 1:37 echoes about Solomon's throne.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the fulfillment of the Davidic covenant theme seen in Solomon's kingship in 1 Kings 1?
options: Acts 2:38
Romans 5:8
Revelation 21:4
questions.explanation: Luke 1:32-33 speaks of Jesus as the Son of David whose kingdom will never end, fulfilling the Davidic covenant theme introduced in 1 Kings 1:37.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'anoint' (מָשַׁח, mashach) imply in the context of Solomon's anointing?
options: To consecrate by pouring oil as a sign of divine selection
To physically heal by applying ointment
To crown with gold and jewels
To declare war
questions.correctAnswer: To consecrate by pouring oil as a sign of divine selection
questions.explanation: The Hebrew verb 'mashach' means to anoint, symbolizing God's choice and consecration of a person for a holy role, as seen in Solomon's anointing in 1 Kings 1:39.

questions.question: How does the episode of Adonijah catching hold of the altar's horns function as a literary device in 1 Kings 1?
options: It functions as an inclusio highlighting sanctuary as refuge
It is a metaphor for rebellion
It illustrates irony of kingship
It shows a prophetic vision
questions.correctAnswer: It functions as an inclusio highlighting sanctuary as refuge
questions.explanation: Adonijah’s taking hold of the altar's horns in 1 Kings 1:50-53 creates an inclusio framing divine sanctuary as a place of asylum, emphasizing the tension between royal power and divine law.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon was present at Adonijah's feast where Adonijah declared himself king.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:10 states that Solomon was not called to Adonijah's feast, showing he was absent when Adonijah proclaimed himself king.

questions.question: True or False: King David was displeased with Adonijah's actions when he prepared chariots and horsemen for himself.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:6 explains that David had not displeased Adonijah or rebuked him for his preparations, indicating David's silence or acceptance at that time.

theological.title: 1 Kings Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Kings Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 1:1 reveal about King David's human frailty and mortality?
options: David was strong and vigorous in his old age
David was old and unable to keep warm despite being clothed
David was healthy but emotionally troubled
David was preparing for war
questions.correctAnswer: David was old and unable to keep warm despite being clothed
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:1 states that King David was old and stricken in years, and although they covered him with clothes, he could not get heat, indicating his human frailty and mortality.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 1:2, what was the purpose of seeking a young virgin for King David?
options: To serve as a political advisor
To cherish and keep the king warm
To train the king's soldiers
To anoint the king
questions.correctAnswer: To cherish and keep the king warm
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 1:2 explains that the servants suggested finding a young virgin to stand before the king, cherish him, and lie in his bosom so that the king might get heat, reflecting the human need for comfort and care.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God's providence can be inferred from the selection of Abishag the Shunammite in 1 Kings 1:3-4?
options: God intervenes directly to prolong life
God provides means for care even in weakness
God abandons the elderly
God chooses only the most powerful servants
questions.correctAnswer: God provides means for care even in weakness
questions.explanation: Verses 3 and 4 show that although David was weak, God’s providence allowed for Abishag to minister to him, demonstrating that God provides means of care during human frailty.

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 1:5-6 reveal the sin of pride through Adonijah’s actions?
options: He humbly waited for his father's blessing
He exalted himself and prepared chariots to claim the throne
He sought God's guidance before acting
He supported Solomon's claim
questions.correctAnswer: He exalted himself and prepared chariots to claim the throne
questions.explanation: Adonijah exalted himself by declaring he would be king and prepared chariots and horsemen, revealing the sin of pride and unlawful ambition (1 Kings 1:5-6).

questions.question: What does the alliance between Adonijah, Joab, and Abiathar in 1 Kings 1:7 teach about human alliances in the face of sin?
options: Sinful ambition often gains support from influential figures
True alliances are based on humility
God approves all human alliances
All alliances are divinely inspired
questions.correctAnswer: Sinful ambition often gains support from influential figures
questions.explanation: Adonijah conferred with Joab and Abiathar who followed him, showing how sinful ambition can attract influential supporters (1 Kings 1:7).

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 1:8 contrast the supporters of Adonijah with those loyal to David's true successor?
options: All Israel supported Adonijah
David’s loyalists included Zadok, Benaiah, and Nathan, opposing Adonijah
Adonijah had no supporters
David supported Adonijah’s claim
questions.correctAnswer: David’s loyalists included Zadok, Benaiah, and Nathan, opposing Adonijah
questions.explanation: Verse 8 lists Zadok, Benaiah, Nathan, and others as not being with Adonijah, implying their loyalty to God’s chosen successor Solomon.

questions.question: What theological insight about divine election and human rejection is illustrated by Adonijah's feast in 1 Kings 1:9-10?
options: Adonijah’s feast confirmed his legitimate kingship
Excluding Solomon shows the rejection of God’s elect
All the king's sons were invited equally
The feast was a religious ceremony
questions.correctAnswer: Excluding Solomon shows the rejection of God’s elect
questions.explanation: Adonijah called all the king’s sons except Solomon to his feast, symbolizing human rejection of God’s elect, as Solomon was the divinely appointed heir (1 Kings 1:9-10).

questions.question: Synthesis: How do 1 Kings 1:11-14 together demonstrate the role of prophetic advocacy in divine kingship?
options: Prophets remain silent in political matters
Nathan advises Bathsheba to remind David of God’s promise, showing prophetic intervention
Prophets support whichever claimant appears strongest
Prophets are irrelevant to royal succession
questions.correctAnswer: Nathan advises Bathsheba to remind David of God’s promise, showing prophetic intervention
questions.explanation: Nathan’s counsel to Bathsheba to remind David of his oath concerning Solomon reveals the prophet’s role as God’s advocate in securing divine kingship (1 Kings 1:11-14).

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 1:17-21, what doctrinal theme about God's covenant faithfulness is emphasized?
options: God breaks His promises to His people
God’s covenant promises must be publicly affirmed to prevent injustice
David had no covenant with Solomon
Adonijah was the true covenant heir
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant promises must be publicly affirmed to prevent injustice
questions.explanation: Bathsheba reminds David of his oath that Solomon would reign, highlighting the necessity of affirming God's covenant to uphold justice and prevent usurpation (1 Kings 1:17-21).

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in David’s oath in 1 Kings 1:29-30 regarding Solomon’s succession?
options: God’s omnipotence to enforce earthly laws
God’s faithfulness to His promises
God’s indifference to human kingship
God’s favoritism towards Adonijah
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness to His promises
questions.explanation: David swears by the LORD who redeemed his soul that Solomon will reign, demonstrating God's faithfulness to keep His promises (1 Kings 1:29-30).

questions.question: Narrative arc: How does the anointing of Solomon in 1 Kings 1:32-39 connect to the greater redemptive story of Scripture?
options: It signifies the rejection of God’s plan
It foreshadows the Messianic kingship fulfilled in Christ
It is merely a political event with no spiritual significance
It indicates the end of divine promises
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the Messianic kingship fulfilled in Christ
questions.explanation: Solomon’s anointing as king foreshadows the ultimate Messianic King, Jesus Christ, who fulfills God’s kingdom promises (1 Kings 1:32-39; Luke 1:32).

questions.question: Synthesis: What combined teaching do 1 Kings 1:40-46 and 1 Kings 1:49-53 convey about God's sovereignty in kingship?
options: God allows human rebellion to determine leaders
God sovereignly establishes His chosen king despite opposition
God’s authority is limited by earthly power
Kingship is entirely a human institution
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly establishes His chosen king despite opposition
questions.explanation: These verses show the public acclamation of Solomon as king against Adonijah’s opposition, illustrating God’s sovereign control over kingship (1 Kings 1:40-46, 49-53).

questions.question: Doctrine: What does 1 Kings 1:50-52 teach about justice and mercy in Solomon’s reign?
options: Solomon executes all his rivals without mercy
Solomon promises mercy to the repentant and justice to the wicked
Solomon ignores threats to his throne
Solomon grants unconditional pardon to Adonijah
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon promises mercy to the repentant and justice to the wicked
questions.explanation: Solomon declares that if Adonijah proves worthy, he will not be harmed, but if wickedness is found, he will die, demonstrating balanced justice and mercy (1 Kings 1:50-52).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the political intrigues in 1 Kings 1 undermine the idea of divine kingship. What does 1 Kings 1:5-7, 32-35 actually teach about God's sovereign appointment of rulers?
options: God has no role in kingship and human politics is chaotic
Despite human scheming, God’s sovereign will prevails in appointing Solomon
Adonijah was the rightful king but rejected by God
Prophets are powerless in political matters
questions.correctAnswer: Despite human scheming, God’s sovereign will prevails in appointing Solomon
questions.explanation: Although Adonijah conspired for the throne, God’s sovereignty is demonstrated as David commands Solomon’s anointing, showing divine election prevails over human ambition (1 Kings 1:5-7, 32-35; Psalm 75:6-7).

questions.question: Attribute question: Which attribute of God is most clearly seen in Nathan’s role as described in 1 Kings 1:23-27?
options: God’s omnipresence
God’s justice and faithfulness in upholding His promises
God’s wrath without mercy
God’s silence in human affairs
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice and faithfulness in upholding His promises
questions.explanation: Nathan, as God’s prophet, confronts David about Adonijah’s claims, reflecting God’s justice and faithfulness in ensuring His promises to Solomon are fulfilled (1 Kings 1:23-27).
